41.0.s.en: 1-2 The Holy Place and the Holy of Holies:

41.0.0.en: 1 Afterward he brought me to the temple, and measured the posts, six cubits broad on the one side, and six cubits broad on the other side, which was the breadth of the tabernacle. 2 And the breadth of the door was ten cubits; and the sides of the door were five cubits on the one side, and five cubits on the other side: and he measured the length thereof, forty cubits: and the breadth, twenty cubits. 3 Then went he inward, and measured the post of the door, two cubits; and the door, six cubits; and the breadth of the door, seven cubits. 4 So he measured the length thereof, twenty cubits; and the breadth, twenty cubits, before the temple: and he said unto me, This is the most holy place. 5 After he measured the wall of the house, six cubits; and the breadth of every side chamber, four cubits, round about the house on every side. 6 And the side chambers were chamber over chamber, thirty-three times; and they entered into the wall which was of the house for the side chambers round about, that they might have hold, but they had not hold in the wall of the house. 7 And there was an enlarging, and a winding about still upward to the side chambers: for the winding about of the house went still upward round about the house: therefore the breadth of the house was still upward, and so increased from the lowest chamber to the highest by the midst. 8 I saw also the height of the house round about: the foundations of the side chambers were a full reed of six great cubits. 9 The thickness of the wall, which was for the side chamber without, was five cubits: and that which was left was the place of the side chambers that were within. 10 And between the chambers was the wideness of twenty cubits round about the house on every side. 11 And the doors of the side chambers were toward the place that was left, one door toward the north, and another door toward the south: and the breadth of the place that was left was five cubits round about.

41.0.1.en: It appears that the dimensions of the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies are as follows:

41.1.0.en: The Holy Place is 40 cubits x 20 cubits [2], while the dimensions of the Holy of Holies are 20 cubits x 20 cubits [4]. However, these figures seem to include the chambers surrounding the building on every side [5]: on the north, the south and the west (for the east is the door or entrance). Thus the dimensions of the whole building, except for the east, are (60 cubits on the north, 60 cubits on the south, and 20 cubits on the west). If the breadth of the surrounding chambers is 4 cubits, then the building contained 33 chambers [6] surrounding the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies on three sides: 15 chambers on the north, 15 chambers on the south, and 3 chambers on the west (since two chambers were taken from the two sides, toward the north and the south).

41.1.1.en: It is noticed that the door is very wide (10 cubits) [2], so that all may enter into the sanctuaries of God and all humanity may enjoy the divine embrace. It is also noticed in [3] that the prophet Ezekiel did not enter the Holy of Holies, for he did not say, "He brought me inward..." but he said, "Then went he inward..." For the Holy of Holies is entered by the high priest alone, once a year, a reference to the Lord Christ, the greatest High Priest, who alone is able to enter into the bosom of the Father, offering the blood of Himself as an atonement for our sins, so that we may enter by Him and in Him!

41.1.2.en: The thirty-three chambers that surrounded the whole building may refer to the humanity of the Lord Christ, in which the divinity was hidden, and through which the believers dwell as members of His mystical body.

41.2.0.en: 12 Now the building that was before the separate place at the end toward the west was seventy cubits broad; and the wall of the building was five cubits thick round about, and the length thereof ninety cubits. 13 So he measured the house, an hundred cubits long; and the separate place, and the building, with the walls thereof, an hundred cubits long; 14 Also the breadth of the face of the house, and of the separate place toward the east, an hundred cubits. 15 And he measured the length of the building over against the separate place which was behind it, and the galleries thereof on the one side and on the other side, an hundred cubits, with the inner temple, and the porches of the court;

41.2.1.en: At the far west, beside the wall, stands a huge building (90 cubits x 70 cubits) that was perhaps used as a storehouse. Some see in it a prophecy of the existence of another building, the Church of the Gentiles, which was in God's eyes awaiting the appointed time to enjoy membership in the body of Christ through faith in Him.

41.3.0.en: 16 The door posts, and the narrow windows, and the galleries round about on their three stories, over against the door, ceiled with wood round about, and from the ground up to the windows, and the windows were covered; 17 To that above the door, even unto the inner house, and without, and by all the wall round about within and without, by measure.

41.3.1.en: The building was supported by walls very thick at the base, less thick in the middle, and thinner still at the top. Thus the higher we go, the thinner the wall becomes, and consequently the breadth of the building increases [7]. This is the condition of the Christian: the higher his heart is raised to heaven, the lighter the weight of his body (the wall) becomes, and his heart within it grows wide with love, and his soul grows even wider, so that the Lord may dwell in it with His Kingdom and His glories.

41.3.2.en: The Lord Christ took our body, hiding behind our wall (Song 2:9), yet He did not bear it heavy with sins, but was like us in all things except sin alone. Therefore His body was light, not in the material sense but in the spiritual sense: He walked on the water and did not sink (Mt 14:25). As for the Apostle Peter, when the sin of doubt entered his heart, he became a dense or heavy body and almost sank. But the Lord, taking him by the hand, lifted him up to Himself, and he became light, so that the waters could not drown him. So also did the prophet Elisha, who cast the stick (the Cross of Christ) into the water, and the heavy iron axe head floated on the face of the water. It is as though we do not need to cast off the body, which is the wall, but that it should be sanctified by our union with the body of Christ, so that our nature is blessed in Him, and our body becomes very light and our heart widens for His Kingdom.

41.3.3.en: The whole building inside, the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, was covered with wood above the windows and below them, and on the walls, and so on... [16-17], so that the whole building would appear from within as one piece of wood, behind which the various stones are hidden. This is a declaration of the unity of the one body of Christ, or of our rising all together as one body hidden behind the Cross, none of us distinguishing himself from another. For in the Cross, as I have said before, a lengthwise unity and a breadthwise unity are accomplished: the unity of heaven with earth, and the unity of those on earth with one another. St. Irenaeus says in this regard: [He who gathers all things into Himself was hung upon a tree.] St. Gregory bishop of Nyssa says: [The Cross is the way that binds the world together.] St. Cyril of Jerusalem says: [The Lord stretched out His hands on the Cross to embrace the ends of the world.] And St. Hippolytus of Rome says: [The Cross is Jacob's ladder; this tree with its heavenly dimensions rose from earth to heaven. It set itself up as an eternal planting between heaven and earth, in order to lift up the world... and to join together different kinds of human nature.]

41.4.0.en: 18 And it was made with cherubims and palm trees, so that a palm tree was between a cherub and a cherub; and every cherub had two faces; 19 So that the face of a man was toward the palm tree on the one side, and the face of a young lion toward the palm tree on the other side: it was made through all the house round about. 20 From the ground unto above the door were cherubims and palm trees made, and on the wall of the temple.

41.4.1.en: The two elements of the ornament are the cherub and the palm tree: a palm tree between cherub and cherub, and every cherub with two faces: the face of a man on this side and the face of a young lion on that side [18-19]. This is a wonderful picture of the Church, which includes holy humanity in the Lord (the palm trees) united with the heavenly ones, who do not stand passive but look toward us, beholding with a face like the face of a man, that is, they share our feelings, and like the face of a young lion, a sign of their spiritual strength and their help to us in Christ Jesus.

41.5.s.en: 6. The altar of incense and the table:

41.5.0.en: 21 The posts of the temple were squared, and the face of the sanctuary; the appearance of the one as the appearance of the other. 22 The altar of wood was three cubits high, and the length thereof two cubits; and the corners thereof, and the length thereof, and the walls thereof, were of wood: and he said unto me, This is the table that is before the LORD.

41.5.1.en: The altar of incense appears here made of wood, because it signifies our prayers that are raised in the presence of God through the Cross. The table signifies the altar of the New Testament, on which the sacrifice of the Eucharist, the bread of life, is offered.

41.6.0.en: 23 And the temple and the sanctuary had two doors. 24 And the doors had two leaves apiece, two turning leaves; two leaves for the one door, and two leaves for the other door. 25 And there were made on them, on the doors of the temple, cherubims and palm trees, like as were made upon the walls; and there were thick planks upon the face of the porch without. 26 And there were narrow windows and palm trees on the one side and on the other side, on the sides of the porch, and upon the side chambers of the house, and thick planks.

41.6.1.en: Here the doors are wider than those of the old temple, because the way to heaven has been opened before all the Gentiles through the preaching of the Gospel.

41.6.3.en: * Set up within me the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, that You may dwell in me, and my heart be filled with love for Your saints and Your angels!

41.6.4.en: * What are these thirty-three chambers surrounding the temple, but a symbol of Your humanity, O You who lived among us these years?!

41.6.5.en: * What is this wide door, but that every person may find a place and enter into the bosom of Your Father?!

41.6.6.en: * The building of Your temple is wondrous:

41.6.7.en: It begins very thick at the bottom, and with every rise the thickness lessens...

41.6.8.en: Will You, then, lift up my heart, so that the weight of the body is removed from me!

41.6.9.en: I shall become light, carried by the Spirit, and the waters of the world will not be able to swallow me!

41.6.10.en: You surrounded the whole building with wood, so it became a wondrous unity, like one piece of wood!

41.6.11.en: Surround me and my brethren with the wood of the Cross, the giver of unity and reconciliation!

41.6.12.en: You adorned the temple of my heart with units of cherubim and palm trees, as though the adornment of my heart were the union of the heavenly ones with the saints (the palm trees)!

41.6.13.en: Every cherub has two faces: the face of a man and the face of a young lion.

41.6.14.en: I see the heavenly ones as men who share my love; I see them as young lions who keep me with strength.

41.6.15.en: Glory to You, who have bound us to Your heavenly creation!

41.6.16.en: * How beautiful is the wooden altar of incense!

41.6.17.en: On it I offer my prayers in the merits of the wood of the Cross!

41.6.19.en: For I am satisfied with Your holy Body and Your precious Blood!

41.6.20.en: * How wide are the doors of Your new temple!

41.6.21.en: They open indeed to call every human being to the heavenly life of the Gospel!

42.0.0.en: 1 Then he brought me forth into the utter court, the way toward the north: and he brought me into the chamber that was over against the separate place, and which was before the building toward the north. 2 Before the length of an hundred cubits was the north door, and the breadth was fifty cubits. 3 Over against the twenty cubits which were for the inner court, and over against the pavement which was for the utter court, was gallery against gallery in three stories. 4 And before the chambers was a walk of ten cubits breadth inward, a way of one cubit; and their doors toward the north. 5 Now the upper chambers were shorter: for the galleries were higher than these, than the lower, and than the middlemost of the building. 6 For they were in three stories, but had not pillars as the pillars of the courts: therefore the building was straitened more than the lowest and the middlemost from the ground. 7 And the wall that was without over against the chambers, toward the utter court on the forepart of the chambers, the length thereof was fifty cubits. 8 For the length of the chambers that were in the utter court was fifty cubits: and, lo, before the temple were an hundred cubits. 9 And from under these chambers was the entry on the east side, as one goeth into them from the utter court. 10 The chambers were in the thickness of the wall of the court toward the east, over against the separate place, and over against the building. 11 And the way before them was like the appearance of the chambers which were toward the north, as long as they, and as broad as they: and all their goings out were both according to their fashions, and according to their doors. 12 And according to the doors of the chambers that were toward the south was a door in the head of the way, even the way directly before the wall toward the east, as one entereth into them.

42.1.0.en: After the prophet Ezekiel had enjoyed entering the Holy Place, which represents the place of communal worship, and the Holy of Holies, which he saw without entering because it represents the atoning work of the Lord Christ by which He brings us into the bosom of the Father, the Spirit led him outside to a building toward the north and another toward the south, representing the chambers (rooms) belonging to the priests, which he called "holy chambers" [13]. These chambers, within the walls of the temple, have their own sanctity, are inseparable from the building of the temple itself and complete it. They represent private worship in the chamber. For the true spiritual life, or union with God in His Son by the Holy Spirit, is not attained by communal worship alone, nor by private worship alone, but is accomplished through worship as one life that a person practices with the congregation as a living member of it, and practices with his family and in his solitude without withdrawing from his membership in the congregation. This is our Church's understanding of the life of worship: it is one life that the believer lives; he takes part with his brethren in worship through his personal, secret relationship with God, and worships in his chamber as a living member of the holy congregation... meaning that there is no duality in worship, communal and individual, but an integrated and inseparable unity.

42.1.1.en: The building was wider in the middle than at the bottom, and increased in breadth in the upper part, because the thickness of the wall of the building lessened as it rose, giving breadth to the upper stories. As we said in the previous chapter, the higher a person rises by the Holy Spirit, the lighter the weight of the needs of the body and its earthly, temporal desires (the wall) becomes, and the heart widens with love.

42.1.2.en: Perhaps the existence of three stories [3, 6], lower chambers, upper chambers, and a third in the middle, reminds us of what the scholar Origen said in speaking of the three kinds of interpretation of the word of God. The bitter literal interpretation represents the lower story, where the space is narrow and the wall very thick, for it makes the soul narrow and the mind not spacious while the body is heavy. In the upper, spiritual interpretation the soul is released into the bridal chamber of the Bridegroom, learns His secrets, and its heart widens with love, and the body is no burden to it. The third interpretation, the behavioral one, stands in the middle. Origen also saw that these three interpretations apply to Noah's ark with its three stories: the lower story holds the unclean animals, the middle the holy animals, and the third, upper story holds Noah and his family on high in fellowship with God.

42.1.3.en: Though the house was wholly covered with wood so as to appear as one piece, one body in the crucified Christ, these many chambers accompany the house as an inseparable part of it to declare that in glory, even though we all form one body, "one star differeth from another star in glory" in the resurrection of the dead (1 Cor 15:41). Truly each rejoices to be in the bosom of the Father, united in His Son by the Holy Spirit, and each rejoices in the glory of his brethren, because of the surpassing nature of the love that works in us there without hindrance; yet "There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars" (1 Cor 15:41). In heaven St. Mary the Mother of God appears glorified above the heavenly and the earthly ones, and the Apostles, disciples, prophets and martyrs appear with their glories because of their sufferings and their witness to God even to the shedding of blood, and so on...

42.1.4.en: The Lord says: "In my Father's house are many mansions" (Jn 14:2). Therefore each one of us strives, not to surpass his brethren in glory, but to attain a deeper fellowship with God and union in Him, that we may reach "unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ" (Eph 4:13).

42.2.0.en: 13 Then said he unto me, The north chambers and the south chambers, which are before the separate place, they be holy chambers, where the priests that approach unto the LORD shall eat the most holy things: there shall they lay the most holy things, and the meat offering, and the sin offering, and the trespass offering; for the place is holy. 14 When the priests enter therein, then shall they not go out of the holy place into the utter court, but there they shall lay their garments wherein they minister; for they are holy; and shall put on other garments, and shall approach to those things which are for the people.

42.2.1.en: The priests use these chambers for two things:

42.2.2.en: A. In them the priests who approach God eat.

42.2.3.en: B. In them are placed the priestly garments for the divine service.

42.2.4.en: It is as though our meeting with the Lord Christ in our chambers aims at our entering into fellowship and practical experience with God, so that we eat His word and are satisfied and refreshed, in order to grow every day in the new life that has become ours in Him. And also that we put on Christ as the garment of righteousness, by whom alone we are able to meet with the Father, so that He accepts our prayers, our fasts and all our worship in Christ Jesus our Lord.

42.3.s.en: 3. The dimensions of the whole house:

42.3.0.en: 15 Now when he had made an end of measuring the inner house, he brought me forth toward the gate whose prospect is toward the east, and measured it round about. 16 He measured the east side with the measuring reed, five hundred reeds, with the measuring reed round about. 17 He measured the north side, five hundred reeds, with the measuring reed round about. 18 He measured the south side, five hundred reeds, with the measuring reed. 19 He turned about to the west side, and measured five hundred reeds with the measuring reed. 20 He measured it by the four sides: it had a wall round about, five hundred reeds long, and five hundred broad, to make a separation between the sanctuary and the profane place.

42.3.1.en: He measured the dimensions of the whole house and found it exceedingly wide, 500 reeds of measure on every side. It is a square house, as seen by St. John the Beloved (Rev 21), and wide enough for all humanity; everyone can find a place in it.

42.4.0.en: Despite its breadth, which declares how much God longs to gather all humanity into it, He made for it a wall "to make a separation between the sanctuary and the profane place" [20]. God's love, His long-suffering and the breadth of His Kingdom do not mean that the unworthy may enter, the careless and those who do not repent to Him.

42.4.2.en: * What is this outer building attached to the temple, but the worship of the chamber that accompanies communal worship?!

42.4.3.en: Teach me to worship You in the midst of the congregation, and to meet with You in secret!

42.4.4.en: In the midst of the congregation I guard my personal relationship with You, and in my chamber I guard my prayer for the sake of the congregation!

42.4.5.en: * What are these three stories of the outer building, but the ladder that lifts me up to enjoy union with You?!

42.4.6.en: Carry me from the narrow and thick lower story, lift me up on high, that I may delight in the breadth of heart and the lightness of spirit!

42.4.7.en: Give me the wings of a dove, that I may fly to heaven!

42.4.8.en: * What do the priests do in this building?

42.4.9.en: They eat what is permitted to them, and put on the garments!

42.4.12.en: By You we are satisfied, and in You we are hidden, O Lover of mankind!
